title: A chat turn keeps what it took: the close carries its steps, tool calls and failed calls, read off its own events, and tracy-web keeps them by the newest close
steps: S1: A turn's log with two steps, four calls: one answer ok:false with isError false, one with the error flag, one ok:true list whose items say ok:false, one plain text.
S2: Close three turns through the turn book: one stopping, one swept by idle, one whose log has no step.
S3: POST /moment work to tracy-web: refused shapes, then closes filed out of order and a retry with none.
expect: S1: {steps: 2, calls: 4, failedCalls: 2}; another turn's events are not counted; no step logged reads null.
S2: the first two closes carry work; the third sends none.

S3: a work without a turn, missing a count, negative, fractional, over 10000 or with more failed than calls is refused before any job; the newest close's work is kept, an older one heard late writes nothing over it, a close without work keeps it; a turn closed by an older dsh reads null.
evidence: Plan tasks/todo-do-dung-that.md U1: a turn's steps and refused calls lived only in dsh's session log (scripts/agent-turn-cost.mjs read them from the container), so no usage view could say how hard a turn was
fence: A failure is the top-level ok:false of a call's answer or its error flag, never a nested ok:false; unknown is null, never zero

tests: none sent → null; whole counts → kept
refused: no turn, not an object
work is written by the newest close
a turn closed by an older dsh reads null work
